skill.name: operating-production-services
skill.description:
SRE patterns for production service reliability: SLOs, error budgets, postmortems, and incident response.
Use when defining reliability targets, writing postmortems, implementing SLO alerting, or establishing
on-call practices. NOT for initial service development (use scaffolding skills instead).
skill.summary: Define reliability targets, manage error budgets, design SLO alerts, and run blameless postmortems.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

content.value_statement: Production teams need clear reliability targets and repeatable incident practices. This skill provides SLO guidance, burn-rate alert patterns, and blameless postmortem templates.
actual_capabilities: Define the SLA, SLO, and SLI hierarchy and choose realistic availability or latency targets.
Calculate error budgets and apply response policies based on remaining budget.
Draft PromQL SLIs and multi-window burn-rate alerts for Prometheus.
Produce standard or quick blameless postmortems with timelines and assigned actions.
Structure 60-minute postmortem meetings and identify reliability anti-patterns.
limitations: Provides reference patterns, not live monitoring, deployment, or incident automation.
Example metric names and thresholds require adaptation and validation for each service.
The slow-burn alert references a 30-minute series not defined in the included recording rules.
The verification script checks file structure and headings only; it does not validate PromQL.

use_cases.title: Set service objectives
use_cases.description: Define measurable availability and latency objectives, then connect them to error-budget policies.

use_cases.title: Build actionable alerts
use_cases.description: Adapt Prometheus recording rules and multi-window burn-rate alerts for an existing service.

use_cases.title: Lead incident learning
use_cases.description: Turn incident facts into a blameless postmortem, clear timeline, root-cause analysis, and owned actions.

prompt_templates.title: Define a basic SLO
prompt_templates.prompt: For [service], define one availability SLI, a realistic 28-day SLO, and the resulting monthly error budget. Explain each choice.

prompt_templates.title: Create an error-budget policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an error-budget policy for [service] with actions above 50%, from 10-50%, below 10%, and at exhaustion.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a postmortem
prompt_templates.prompt: Using these incident facts: [facts], draft a blameless postmortem with summary, UTC timeline, 5 Whys, impact, and owned action items.

prompt_templates.title: Design multi-window alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: For [service metrics] and [SLO target], propose Prometheus availability and latency SLIs, recording rules, and fast and slow burn-rate alerts. State assumptions.

output_examples.input: Our API requires 99.9% monthly availability. Create an error-budget policy.
A deployment caused 20 minutes of errors and rollback restored service. Draft a postmortem outline.
output_examples.output: The outline includes an executive summary, UTC timeline, customer impact, 5 Whys analysis, immediate correction, and assigned prevention actions.

output_examples.input: Propose an alert strategy for a 99.9% availability SLO.
output: Use a fast-burn alert to detect rapid budget consumption.
Use a slow-burn alert to catch sustained degradation.
Validate thresholds with historical traffic before paging.

best_practices: Replace example metric names, targets, and thresholds with validated service data.
Connect every postmortem action to an owner, due date, and tracking ticket.
Review burn-rate alerts against historical incidents before paging the on-call team.
anti_patterns: Do not adopt 100% SLOs without considering cost and error budgets.
Do not page directly on raw SLIs when burn-rate context is available.
Do not use postmortems to blame individuals or create unowned actions.

faq.question: Does this skill configure monitoring systems?
faq.answer: No. It supplies guidance and templates; teams must adapt, validate, and deploy configurations in their own environments.

faq.question: Which monitoring stack do the examples target?
faq.answer: The examples use Prometheus metrics and recording rules, plus Grafana dashboard concepts.

faq.question: Can this skill manage an active incident?
faq.answer: It supports documentation and review, but does not replace incident command, diagnostics, escalation, or recovery procedures.

faq.question: How should teams choose SLO targets?
faq.answer: Start from customer expectations and business risk, then balance desired reliability against cost and delivery needs.

faq.question: Does the verification script validate alerts?
faq.answer: No. The script only confirms required files and section names. PromQL and alert behavior require separate testing.

faq.question: Which postmortem formats are included?
faq.answer: The skill includes standard and quick templates, a 5 Whys section, action-item tracking, and a 60-minute meeting guide.
